pr.title: Color the review labels as the panel draws their states, and have init bring Projector's labels up to date
pr.head: 8492817358104d0c2122380e708a69f85afc7886

summary: Projector puts two labels on a pull request while it reviews it: reviewing while a review runs, and clean once the newest review of the head found nothing. The review commands create each label the first time a repository needs it, and Projector's panel in Claude Code shows the same two states and, in its drawer, each pull request's labels in their GitHub colors.

The label colors did not match the panel. The panel draws reviewing in Claude's orange and clean in the theme's success green, but the labels were created yellow (fbca04) and a darker green (0e8a16). This change gives the labels the panel's dark-theme colors, d77757 and 4eba65.

A new default alone reaches only repositories that do not have the labels yet, because the review commands never change a label that exists. So project init gains a step that brings the labels up to date:

• A missing label is created with Projector's color and description.
  • A label that still has an old Projector color and Projector's description is recolored, because nobody chose that color.
  • Any other label, one whose color or description someone changed, stays as it is.
The step runs whatever the answer to init's required-check question, prints a line for each change, warns rather than fails when GitHub refuses, and does nothing when review.labels is false.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review found that the existing InitSiteTests ran the real gh api label listing, 38 calls per run. The tests now fake those calls, and SiteRepoCase fails any gh call a test does not fake. A full-suite run with a logging stub gh recorded no calls.
  • Its three suggestions were taken: a clearer test comment, a plural in the docs, and a rewrapped paragraph.
  • The review of this head is clean, and the gate passed, including CI's check job.

groups.title: The label colors and the update step
groups.kicker: The new colors, the colors an earlier release used, and the step that moves one to the other
intro: review.LABELS holds each label's color and description, and the review commands create a label from it the first time a pull request needs one. FORMER_LABEL_COLORS lists the colors an earlier release created each label with, so sync_labels can tell a color Projector chose from one a person chose.
init_labels in the CLI runs sync_labels as the last step of project init, after the required-check step, and only when the checkout's origin is on GitHub.

checks.text: A label counts as Projector's own only while both its color is an old Projector color and its description is Projector's exact text. Changing either one makes it the repository's label, which init never touches.

files.note: The new colors, the list of former colors, and sync_labels, which lists a repository's labels and creates or recolors Projector's.

checks.text: The name is matched lowercased, the color is compared lowercased, and the description is compared exactly, so a label GitHub reports as FBCA04 is recolored and one renamed Reviewing with another description is left. LabelSyncTests covers both, and passed at this head.

files.note: init_labels, which skips a checkout without a GitHub origin and a repository with review.labels = false, and turns a refusal from GitHub into a warning.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: A fake GitHub that keeps labels, the label step's three rules, and site tests kept off GitHub
intro: RulesetGitHub, the fake gh the required-check tests already use, now keeps a list of labels and answers the list, create, and update calls. LabelSyncTests runs project init against it.

project init now calls review.run_gh, so the site tests that run init fake it too. SiteRepoCase, the base of the site tests, also replaces every gh entry point with a guard that fails the test, so a call no test fakes cannot reach GitHub with the signed-in account's token.

files.note: LabelSyncTests: a recolor of an untouched label but not of one a person changed, a create of both labels that a rerun does not repeat, and the review.labels = false and refused cases. The required-check tests now leave the label calls out of their "asks GitHub nothing" assertions.
The label that the first review in a repository creates now carries the new orange.

The guard on summary.gh, summary.gh_lookup, and review.run_gh, a fake run_gh on FakeGitHub that lists Projector's labels at their current colors, and a stub of summary.base_pr for the one build test that looked up a stacked pull request.

checks.text: The full suite, run with a logging stub gh first on PATH, passed and recorded no gh calls at this head.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The new init step and the new colors in the CLI reference
intro: docs/cli.md gains the section "Keep the review labels current" under init, and the labels table under "Review a pull request" gives the new colors and the reason for them.

files.note: The new init section, a note that init without a terminal now changes the labels, and the labels table with its new colors.
